question: Does UnitedHealth Group's weekly, daily, and 4-hour price action confirm institutional accumulation, or did the November 2026 breakdown invalidate the prior base?

epigraph.quote: Never confuse an oversold bounce inside a Stage 4 decline with the formation of a durable Stage 1 base.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Discipline

web_blocks.html: UnitedHealth Group suffered severe technical damage during the week ended November 20, 2026. The stock dropped -16.67% on the week (Finviz: -16.59%, 1M: -19.42% to -20.03%) before staging a modest +2.84% dead-cat bounce on Friday to close at $339.85 (TradingView close: $339.88) against Thursday's $330.48 close. Volume surged to 12.78 million shares (TradingView: 12.80 million), representing 2.01x the 20-day average and 1.87x the 30-day average (2.25x Finviz relative volume). That distribution wave sliced cleanly through UNH's 20-day ($394.52), 50-day ($388.70), 200-day ($368.54), and 30-week ($396.67) moving averages in a single week.

web_blocks.title: Stage Split Disclosure: Facts Ledger (Stage 1) vs. Snapshot Screen (Stage 4)

web_blocks.html: Two automated market feeds classify UNH's trend differently on November 20, 2026, and both readings must be disclosed transparently. The market-facts ledger (facts_US_2026-11-20.json) tags UNH as Stage 1 (Basing) with a FALLING/FLAT 50-day SMA ($388.70 vs. $390.65 ten sessions earlier) and 7 distribution days in the trailing 25 sessions. By contrast, the TradingView snapshot screen (snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json) assigns STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN) because price ($339.85 / $339.88) broke -12.56% below the 50-day SMA, -7.78% below the 200-day SMA, and -14.32% below the 30-week SMA. We enforce the stricter STAGE_4 classification because a -16.67% breakdown beneath every major weekly and daily trend floor—alongside a breached prior $358.00 stop and $365.05 breakdown trigger—signals active institutional liquidation rather than quiet basing.

Across all three charting horizons—weekly, daily, and 4-hour—momentum remains fractured with zero confirmed reversal structure. Daily RSI sits at 29.70 (29.69 Finviz) and 4-hour RSI sits at 27.57, signaling short-term oversold stretch without an intraday turn (intraday_4h_turn: false). TradingView rates UNH an overall Sell (-0.31) driven by a Strong Sell (-0.80) moving-average score, while the broader U.S. market sits in a confirmed Downtrend (only 38.8% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day SMA and 10 distribution days). Meanwhile, UNH options carry NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID status in the live options desk audit (bid-ask spreads exceeding 14% or insufficient open interest at current strikes), with zero open option contracts held.

web_blocks.takeaway: Every timeframe from 4-hour to weekly places UNH in a Stage 4 decline inside a 10-distribution-day U.S. Downtrend, confirming that Friday's bounce to $339.85 is an oversold reflex rather than a tradable bottom.

web_blocks.title: Prior Stop-Loss Breach Confirmation ($358.00 Breached at $339.85)
paragraphs: The prior November 17, 2026 spine established a pending breakdown alert at $365.05 and a hard structural invalidation stop at $358.00. At the November 20 close of $339.85, UNH stands $18.15 (-5.07%) below that $358.00 structural stop and $25.20 below the $365.05 alert level. Under portfolio risk rules, holding through a breached stop turns a defined -4.1% risk trade into an open-ended Stage 4 drawdown; all 4.6973 Schwab shares must be exited immediately into cash.

book_paragraphs: Fundamental research tells us what a business is worth over years, while technical structure tells us whether large institutional pools of capital are accumulating or dumping the stock today. For UnitedHealth Group on November 20, 2026, the verdict from the tape is unambiguous: institutional money is leaving the stock rapidly. During the week ending November 20, UNH fell 16.67 percent, closing Friday at $339.85 after touching a 20-day swing low of $324.67. Although shares ticked up 2.84 percent on Friday from Thursday's $330.48 close, trading volume remained heavy at 12.78 million shares—roughly double the 20-day average—indicating high-turnover liquidation rather than quiet support.

To keep our technical diagnosis completely transparent, we must disclose a split between our two automated market feeds. The market-facts ledger still labels UNH as Stage 1 Basing because the 50-day simple moving average sits at $388.70 against $390.65 ten days earlier, alongside seven distribution days in the past 25 sessions. However, the live TradingView snapshot screen assigns Stage 4 with a hard capital rejection gate because price dropped 12.56 percent beneath the 50-day average, 7.78 percent beneath the 200-day average at $368.54, and 14.32 percent beneath the 30-week average at $396.67. Whenever a stock slices more than one average true range below both its 200-day and 30-week averages in a single high-volume week, the stricter Stage 4 classification governs our capital decisions.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Horizons Together
paragraphs: Zooming across three timeframes prevents mistaking a single green day for a durable trend change. On the weekly chart, UNH has fallen 26.38 percent from its 52-week high of $461.62 and trades well beneath its 10-week exponential average ($387.40), 40-week exponential average ($379.57), and 30-week simple average ($396.67). Weekly RSI has cooled to 38.19, leaving ample room before reaching extreme historical washed-out levels. On the daily chart, the 14-day Average True Range expanded to $15.36, meaning normal daily swings now exceed 4.5 percent of the stock price.

On the 4-hour chart, the stock trades far beneath its 4-hour 20-period EMA ($375.04) and 50-period SMA ($399.23), with Bollinger Band width stretched to 28.01 percent. Both daily RSI at 29.70 and 4-hour RSI at 27.57 sit below the traditional 30 oversold threshold, yet the 4-hour trend algorithm records no confirmed upward turn. Oversold conditions explain Friday's bounce near classic Pivot S2 support at $334.76, but oversold stocks routinely bounce sharply inside Stage 4 bear markets only to roll over into lower lows once short-term buyers exhaust themselves.

book_subsections.title: Sector Breadth, Stop Breach & Illiquid Options
paragraphs: Macro and peer context reinforce caution. The broader U.S. equity market sits in a confirmed Downtrend with only 38.8 percent of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day moving averages and 10 institutional distribution days over the past 25 sessions. Only three of eleven S&P sectors hold above their 50-day averages. Within Managed Health Care, Elevance Health and Cigna also sit in Stage 4 downtrends, whereas capital inside healthcare has migrated cleanly toward Stage 2 biopharma and distribution leaders such as Eli Lilly, AbbVie, and McKesson. Selling pressure in UNH reflects an entire industry group falling out of institutional favor.

Finally, our options audit confirms that UNH options fail liquidity gates for tactical hedging or replacement structures, with quoted spreads exceeding 14 percent in the snapshot chain and zero open contracts held. More importantly, our November 17, 2026 baseline had established a breakdown alert at $365.05 and a hard structural invalidation stop at $358.00. At $339.85, the stock closed 5.07 percent below that $358.00 stop. Disciplined risk management never widens a stop on a losing position after a support breach; protecting capital requires accepting the signal and exiting.

book_subsections.title: What a True Stage 1 Base Looks Like From Here
paragraphs: Knowing what is broken today also clarifies exactly what repair looks like tomorrow. Before UnitedHealth Group can become buyable again, selling volume must dry up and shares must stop making lower weekly lows. Ideally, the stock carves out a multi-week or multi-month sideways Stage 1 base around the $300.00 to $325.00 demand zone—roughly one to two average true ranges below classic Pivot S2 at $334.76 and safely above the $255.97 52-week low.

During that basing process, the 50-day simple moving average ($388.70) and 30-week simple moving average ($396.67) need time to flatten out after their current steep decline. A single sharp relief rally back into $365.00 or $375.00 is not a Stage 2 breakout; overhead supply from trapped buyers who accumulated near $380.00 to $410.00 will likely create resistance on initial bounces. Only when UNH breaks upward out of a flat Stage 1 box on above-average institutional volume, reclaims both its 50-day and 30-week averages, and sees S&P 500 breadth climb back above 50 percent will the odds shift back in favor of buyers.

book_subsections.title: Pivot Geometry, Overhead Supply & Institutional Accumulation Signals
paragraphs: Mapping concrete price thresholds helps observers stay patient while Stage 4 plays out. Below Friday's $339.85 close, classic Pivot S2 support sits at $334.76, followed by the 20-day swing low at $324.67 and the 52-week low down at $255.97. Above current price, classic Pivot S1 at $370.86, the 200-day simple moving average at $368.54, the 10-week exponential average at $387.40, and the 50-day simple moving average at $388.70 form a dense band of overhead resistance. Investors who bought shares near $390.00 to $435.00 in October and early November now sit underwater and often sell into rallies just to break even.

Institutional accumulation shows up in footprint metrics long before headline earnings change. When UNH finally bottoms, look for weekly closes to stop making lower lows on lighter volume, followed by high-volume up-weeks that hold above the 10-week and 30-week averages. At the same time, look for S&P 500 distribution days to recede from the current ten-day cluster and for sector peers like Elevance Health and Cigna to stabilize. Until those volume and breadth footprints turn constructive, any bounce remains tactical noise inside a broken trend.

book_callouts.title: Why Oversold RSI Is Not a Buy Signal in Stage 4
book_callouts.text: When daily RSI drops below 30, it measures speed of recent selling, not the end of a downtrend. In Stage 4 declines, stocks can stay oversold for weeks or repeatedly bounce into declining 20-day and 50-day averages before making fresh lows. Real bottoms require sideways basing and rising volume accumulation, not a single oversold tick.
